_camera: Where the pack's camera sits in its rig, metres, the rig facing +z: its FPSPlayer prefab's Camera (field of view 80, near 0.01) at 0.012, 1.654, 0.06, 9 cm over the head bone. fprig.ts puts it on our eye, so the arms' shoulders stay where the pack made them, just out of the picture; the gun goes where our view puts it and both hands reach it (KINEMATION's own rig: the gun on its weapon bone, the hands on it by IK). Hung off our gun instead, the arms' shoulders and sleeves came into the view and filled a third of it.
_fov: The gun camera's vertical field of view at the hip while these arms hold the gun: the pack's own camera's (its FPSPlayer prefab, field of view 80), which its holds are made to be seen at. Ours at the default setting is 92, and the arms' forearms and the gun's back end, a few centimetres from the eye, filled the bottom of the view. Aimed, the sight picture is every gun's own (main.ts gunFov).
_adsShoulder: Metres both shoulders go back in the sights, on top of the pack gun's own clavicle offset (its settings asset): our sights bring the gun to the eye nearer than KINEMATION's player does (it stops short by the gun's aim point offset, 10 to 12 cm), and with the shoulder where the hold put it the USSO's right wrist bent 109 degrees aimed and its left 70 (tools/e2e.ts, the pack's wristBend).
_hipPitch: The barrel's pitch at rest with these arms, radians up: 0.035, 2 degrees. The fit tilts our gun up about its trigger to meet the pack's left palm, 10 degrees on the USSO and 12 on BOOG (measured), and the muzzle pointed up and to the left standing still; the owner, 2026-09-28: "look at hyperscape and apex, in the chilling / standing position, the gun is never like that". The view takes the tilt back off down to this, the hands following the gun (viewmodel.ts), and keeps every gun's 3 degrees in toward the crosshair.
_sprint: The pack's sprint on the gun (fprig.ts locomotion): its swing, 51 degrees across the body, comes in over `easeIn` s while sprinting and goes over `easeOut` s the moment you fire, aim or reload, and comes back `fireHold` s after the last shot. SpeedKills sprints whenever you move forward, firing included, and with the sprint on by speed alone the owner fired from a gun swung across the body, the tracers nowhere near the crosshair (2026-09-27, the live server). In the sights none of the pack's walk or sprint is kept. `swing` is how much of the pack's sprint (its tactical carry, the gun swung across the chest and rolled on its side) is used: none. SpeedKills sprints whenever you move, and with it on the owner saw the gun "crossed and inverted" the whole time he moved (2026-09-27); the run keeps the ready hold, the walk's bob carried on at a run.
_reload: The reload with the bought arms, the owner's (2026-09-27): "point a finger at it while it phases out and in for a reload and then smack the charging handle ... same with the sniper ... a nice combo of the two". Shares of the reload: the left hand leaves the gun over `point` and points at the magazine, its index finger out and its tip `gap` m off the magazine's left face, the hand `reach` m back from the tip along `aim` (in the gun's frame: right, up, ahead), while the gun turns its underside toward you (gunfeel.json reload.twist); the magazine phases out over `phaseOut` and a new one in over `phaseIn`, staying in the gun, and seats at `seat`; then over `rack` the pack's own hands work the gun: each pack gun's `rack` names the clip and the share of it where they do (measured off its gun clip: the MPS5's empty reload slaps its handle forward at 0.69, the L96X's fire clip works its bolt over 0.30 to 0.48), and the hands go back to the hold. It had been the pack's whole reload, the magazine carried out of the gun to the belt and back, its phase out of sight. `twist` turns the gun while the hand points (radians, and metres before the view's scale), smaller than gunfeel.json's own: at that one the gun filled the middle of the screen and the pointing hand came up to the eye. A pack gun's own `twist` replaces it: the USSO's magazine sits low, and at the shared one its pointing hand was below the screen's edge. Which face of the magazine the finger comes at is `face` (in the gun's frame; -1 on x its left face, -1 on y its bottom), `aim` the way it points, and a pack gun's own `point` replaces the three: the BOOG's magazine is a thin plate low on the gun's left side, and pointed at from its left the hand sat between the eye and it (2026-09-27, a picture with the magazine tinted red), so its finger comes up at its bottom, the gun pitched and rolled more to show it. The pointing arm's elbow bends toward `elbow` from its shoulder (in the view: right, up, toward you), hanging down: bent the way the hold had it, the USSO's point, 22 cm from the shoulder, folded the arm so tight that on the way its elbow passed 9 cm in front of the eye and the sleeve filled the view for a tenth of the reload (measured bone by bone, 2026-09-27). The magazine slides as it phases (the owner, 2026-09-28: "drop out and pixelate, and then pixelate and slide in with a distance from start to end"): the old one `slide` view metres down its own length as it goes, the new one from there up into the gun as it comes (the USSO's is 17 cm long, BOOG's 12 cm tall, measured in the view), and the finger follows it. The fingertip is `shift` view metres left and down of the point it points at (the owner: "down and left more on both, not by too much"), the hand turned `aimAt` of the way from its forearm's line to point at it. From the point the gun goes straight into its rack pose (a pack gun's rack `pose`, view radians and metres) over `rackBlend` of the reload, and a pack gun's rack `gunKeep` is the share of its rack clip's own gun motion kept: the MPS5's empty reload is made for a handle at the front of its gun, and the USSO's is at the back, 35 cm from the eye, so carried over the left hand came to 27 cm and filled a third of the view, the gun thrown small and far to the middle (2026-09-28, every frame of it measured and looked at; tools/pack-frames.ts). The hand points along the line from its shoulder to the fingertip, `bend` of the way toward `aim` (along `aim` alone the wrist bent 107 to 126 degrees), at `at` of the magazine's height from its bottom (its middle, up a pistol grip, is hidden by the other hand). A pack gun's rack `shift` moves a hand while its rack clip works the gun, view metres along our gun's axes: the L96X's right hand throws its bolt where BOOG's body is, the glove 15 mm into it; 18 mm out along the gun's width leaves none of it through the gun where it is seen over the bolt's throw (searched, 2026-09-28, the arms turned with the levelled gun). A pack gun's rack `grab` closes the left hand on our handle itself: the owner, 2026-09-28, "we get close to it, but our fingers don't grip it, it's like 80% of the way there". The USSO's handle is a knob standing a centimetre off the gun's left side, which no closed hand holds without going into the gun (10 mm and more, every roll of the pack's own grip and every turn of a hand closed round it, searched), so it is a `pinch`: the thumb and forefinger's tips (`hook` off the knob, in our gun's frame) on it, the other three fingers curled into the palm, the hand turned with its knuckles `along` and its palm facing `palm` in our gun's frame, and the forefinger `curl` (below 0, opened) from the pack's grip. Searched by what of the hand is through the gun where it is seen, its gap to the gun and its wrist: none through, touching, the wrist 22 degrees.
_swap: On a swap or holster the arms drop out of the picture as the gun phases out, and come back up to take the next one as it phases in (the owner: "the guns fly in and out but the arms stay in a weird position"): at the phase's bottom the whole rig is `drop` m lower, `back` m nearer and pitched `pitch` radians down, about the eye. With `clips` of the pack's own swap on top (fprig.ts swapMotion, its Rifle_Unequip and Rifle_Equip, measured: the gun swung 29 cm across, 34 cm in to the chest and turned 58 degrees, the hands on it all the way), the one into the other over `cross` of the swap either side of its middle, where the guns change; the owner, 2026-09-28: "look for more things we can do with it, especially when we swap guns, what the hands and arms can do". The arms drop only from `dropFrom` of the way out of the picture (the gun all but gone): from the start they left the gun flying on its own while the pack's swap carried it.
_pickup: Taking something off the ground (main.ts applyLoot, any item but a gun, which comes into the hands by the swap): the pack's pickup clip, its left hand down and back up, over `seconds` (the clip's own length), eased in and out over `ease` of it. `gunKeep` is the share of the clip's own motion of the gun kept: all of it tipped the gun up onto its side and bent the right wrist to 88 degrees.
_free: The bought arms off a gun (fprig.ts free, handTurn; the owner, 2026-09-28: the fists were "the old fists and not our new bought arms"). `fist`: each finger joint's bend in a fist, radians, along the axis the pack's own grip bends it (its first gun's pose clip, the right hand round a pistol grip). `palmSign`: which way off the knuckles each hand's palm faces, the hands being mirrored. `palm`: on an inspect, the open left hand's knuckles and the way its palm faces, in the view's space (x right, y up, z back toward the eye), with the hack floating over it. `pull`: the fists moved from the view's own fists' place toward the eye, view metres (in, up, back): the bought arms are shorter than the view's, and there they were straight out, 97% of their reach.
_inspectPalm: Where the open left hand's wrist is on an inspect, view metres (x right, y up, z back toward the eye), and how the hack floats over the palm: `bob` metres up and down at `rate` a second, `spin` radians side to side. `lift`: how far off the palm the hack floats, view metres (at 6 cm it sat in the palm).
_guns: Which pack gun stands in for which of ours, chosen on pictures at the owner's view: the USSO's is the MPS5, a compact SMG held by its handguard, its charging handle worked from empty; the Striker-V, the first tried, holds its long magazine as a grip, 22 cm under where the USSO's short one sits, and the hand could not be on both. BOOG's is the L96X, a bolt sniper that works its bolt after every shot. A pack gun's gun clips list only those the import makes a file of: the MPS5's and the L96X's A_W pose are stills with no animation, which tools/import-fparms.ts writes nothing for, and asked for they were a 404 on every page once the arms load at the start for the fists (the live check caught it, 2026-09-28); the rig runs without them.
